clue.text: Garment for family on pictures?

indicators.note: in an across clue 'family on pictures' puts the family word after the pictures word

parts.note: oils are paintings, pictures done in oil paint
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Someone asks which piece of clothing suits a family posing for photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pictures' suggests photographs, but here they are paintings in oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat made of cloth treated with oil is a garment worn by sailors and fishermen.

clue.text: Managed some cricket on a Wednesday

indicators.note: in a down clue the cricket word sits on top of the following letters

parts.note: overs are sets of six balls in cricket, so some cricket

explanation.surface: Someone played a few overs of cricket on a Wednesday.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or direct is to manage, past tense to match.

clue.text: Grub that was found right inside volcanic rock

indicators.note: the right letter is placed within the rock word

parts.note: lava is molten or solidified volcanic rock

explanation.surface: A grub was discovered tucked into volcanic stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's wormlike immature stage is a grub.

clue.text: First of all, keep all your admirers, knowing your craft

indicators.note: take the first letter of every word that follows

explanation.surface: Advice to retain your fans by mastering your trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of all' looks like 'to begin with', but it means the first letters of all the next five words.
explanation.definitionFit: A small canoe paddled by one person is a boat, a craft.

clue.text: A single check in case of none showing simplicity

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the outer letters of none
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
to vet is to check thoroughly

explanation.surface: A lone cheque inside an empty case shows guilelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of none' gives N and E, the first and last letters of 'none', with AIVET inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent artlessness and lack of worldly experience amount to simplicity.

clue.text: A dimmer sort of marine creature

indicators.note: to sort something is to rearrange it, so the letters of the phrase before are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone describes a rather dimwitted kind of sea animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the seven letters of 'A dimmer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary sea-dweller with a woman's upper body and a fish's tail is a fabled marine being.

clue.text: Mrs dale's cooked fruit

indicators.note: cooking alters what goes in, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Mrs Dale's stewed fruit, as in a cosy kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the letters of 'Mrs dale' (the possessive adds none).
explanation.definitionFit: These are small brown apple-like fruits eaten when half rotten.

clue.text: One maintains a precipitous conclusion

parts.note: rainfall, precipitation, ends up held in a store of water, which keeps a supply in reserve

explanation.surface: Someone insists on a sudden, steep ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precipitous' suggests steepness, but it hints at precipitation, rain, whose end point is a lake that holds water in store.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial lake storing water for supply is where rainfall ends up and is kept.

clue.text: Refraining from taking new bat in nets

indicators.note: a new version of the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A batsman declines to use a new bat in the practice nets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of 'bat in nets'; cricket nets are enclosed practice areas.
explanation.definitionFit: Teetotal or self-denying, someone who holds back from indulging.

clue.text: Me on LSD? Perhaps the stones!

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone on LSD wonders if they are seeing the ancient stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges the letters of 'Me on LSD'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric tombs made of upright slabs topped by a capstone are megalithic structures.

clue.text: Chorus singer making good time?

parts.note: a bird singing in the dawn chorus is up at first light, and so is a punctual person who makes good time

explanation.surface: A choir member who keeps the tempo well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chorus' suggests a choir, but it is the dawn chorus of birds; 'good time' is arriving promptly, not musical rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a bird out at dawn and a person who rises or arrives well ahead of others.

clue.text: Hemp is a pound on Sunday!

indicators.note: in an across clue 'is a pound on Sunday' places those pieces after the Sunday letter

parts.note: L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: An exclamation that hemp costs a pound on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough fibre from an agave plant used for rope, it is a kind of hemp in the broad sense of rope fibre.

clue.text: Southern writer the French put in irons

parts.note: a hack is a writer, especially a journalist turning out copy for pay
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A writer from the American South is put in chains by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' is not a nation acting but the French word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetter someone is to put iron restraints on their limbs, the verb form of a chain cuff.

clue.text: What a deep sea diver needs is planes

definitions.text: What a deep sea diver needs

explanation.surface: Someone explains what a diver must have, and it is aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style diver breathes through a hose from the surface; a company that flies passengers is a carrier operating planes.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver's air supply tube is literally an air line, and a commercial carrier running aircraft is a company of planes.

clue.text: Machine producing drink for journalists?

parts.note: a device that crushes grapes produces drink, and the drink paired with the journalists' collective name gives the phrase

explanation.surface: A machine making beverages for reporters in a newsroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The device crushes grapes, but read whimsically it is wine plus the press, the collective term for journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the apparatus in which grapes are squeezed to extract juice for fermenting.

clue.text: Fliers who enjoy a few evening pints?

definitions.text: who enjoy a few evening pints?

explanation.surface: Birds that like a drink at night.
explanation.walkthrough: A jar is British slang for a pint of beer, so drinkers at night are humorously night jars; the real ones are nocturnal birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal birds with churring calls are fliers, and the second reading is a jokey term for night drinkers.

clue.text: Punishing matches have their drawbacks

parts.note: football matches include punishments for fouls, and such punishments are also disadvantages

explanation.surface: A remark that grueling games have downsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punishing' suggests exhausting, but it means punishments given in matches, which are also handicaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicks awarded for fouls are sporting punishments, and the word also means disadvantages.

clue.text: Competitions for writers on love?

indicators.note: in an across clue 'writers on love' puts the writers word after the love letter

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shown as the letter O
pens are writing instruments, things that write

explanation.surface: Contests held for authors writing about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writers' suggests authors, but they are pens; 'love' is tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournaments in golf and tennis open to all players are called by this name, so they are competitions.

clue.text: One doesn't believe there's silver in the pot

indicators.note: the silver letters are placed inside the pot word

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at a claim that silver lies hidden in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen does not follow the main religions, so is a person lacking that belief.

clue.text: Exercise runs employed and studied

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
used means employed

explanation.surface: Runs were done as exercise and examined closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To read through carefully is to examine or study.

clue.text: Produces teenagers?

parts.note: parents bring young people into being, and the letters of teenagers can be rearranged to give the verb for producing

explanation.surface: A question about what yields adolescents.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the play: teenagers rearranged spells a verb meaning produces, as though making teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about or create something is to produce it.

clue.text: Good answer — tabloid editor's car may so be kept!

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging term for a cheap newspaper
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor's car is well stored, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: a car may be kept this way, under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Housed in a shed for vehicles is how a car is often stored overnight.

clue.text: Figure out meal run

indicators.note: out signals the letters are in disarray, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Work out the cost of a meal run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of 'meal run'; 'Figure out' falsely reads as one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol for a number is a figure, as in a digit.

clue.text: Sort of printing gun — can it lose initially?

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

indicators.note: the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A question whether a kind of printing gun can fail at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten was a British submachine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing through a cut-out template is a method of producing lettering and designs.

clue.text: Rubber tail on baby's toy snake!

indicators.note: in an across clue the tail letter goes on after the toy word

parts.note: a rattle is a noise-making toy for babies

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, here of rubber

explanation.surface: A rubber tail is attached to a baby's toy snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber tail' reads as a rubber appendage, but it is only the final letter of 'Rubber'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is informally named for the rattling segments on its tail.

clue.text: China captured revolutionary weapon

indicators.note: the friend word holds the revolutionary inside it

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a friend
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: China seized a revolutionary new kind of weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy blade used for cutting through vegetation can serve as a weapon.

clue.text: Run out of gear?

parts.note: a car rolling along without power, with the engine disengaged, is moving freely

explanation.surface: Someone has exhausted their kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' suggests exhausting a supply; here it is moving along with the gears disengaged.
explanation.definitionFit: To freewheel downhill is to move without propulsion.

clue.text: Fear going topless may be a mistake

indicators.note: the top letter, the first in a down clue, is removed

parts.note: terror is extreme fear

explanation.surface: Fear of going topless might be misguided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' removes the first letter of TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or slip is an error of judgment.

clue.text: Crawled in front of singular teacher!

indicators.note: the swimming word comes before the singular letter

parts.note: to crawl is to swim the front crawl stroke, so swam
singular gives I, the numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone crept up before a remarkable teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawled' suggests creeping, but it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious master or guru is a spiritual teacher.

clue.text: Good criteria for re-housing an old person

indicators.note: the letters of criteria are moved into a new home, rearranged

explanation.surface: Sound standards for moving an elderly person to new accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for re-housing' rearranges CRITERIA into ERIATRIC, after G.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used, often disparagingly, for an elderly individual.

clue.text: Neglected and treated with contempt outside university

indicators.note: the contempt word sits around the university letter

parts.note: dissed is slang for disrespected

explanation.surface: Someone was ignored and scorned beyond the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer used is abandoned and left idle.

clue.text: Delayed — and real energy lost by the side

parts.note: late means delayed or behind time

indicators.note: the energy letter is removed from the word real

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone, running behind, has run out of steam on the sidelines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes E out of 'real', leaving RAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideways or positioned at the flank means to one side.
